validated_results.title: Risk of prostate cancer in African-American men: Evidence of mixed effects of dietary quercetin by serum vitamin D status.
validated_results.reason: Original human case-control analysis reporting age-adjusted odds ratios for dietary quercetin intake and prostate cancer occurrence in African-American men.

extraction.comparison_type: Increased dietary quercetin intake among men with vitamin D deficiency (age-adjusted)
extraction.population: African-American men aged 40-70 with prostate cancer undergoing treatment and controls from a free prostate cancer screening program

sample_size.excerpt: Participants included 90 AA men with PCa undergoing treatment at Howard University Hospital (HUH) and 62 controls participating in HUH's free PCa screening program.
sample_size.location: abstract; total_n derived from reported group counts 90 + 62 = 152

cases.excerpt: Participants included 90 AA men with PCa undergoing treatment at Howard University Hospital (HUH) and 62 controls participating in HUH's free PCa screening program.

effect_size.excerpt: In individuals with vitD deficiency, increased dietary quercetin showed a tendency toward lower risk of PCa (OR = 0.91, 95%CI: 0.82-1.00; P = 0.054, age-adjusted) while men with normal vitD were at elevated risk (OR = 1.23, 95%CI: 1.04-1.45).

confidence_interval.excerpt: In individuals with vitD deficiency, increased dietary quercetin showed a tendency toward lower risk of PCa (OR = 0.91, 95%CI: 0.82-1.00; P = 0.054, age-adjusted) while men with normal vitD were at elevated risk (OR = 1.23, 95%CI: 1.04-1.45).

comparison.excerpt: In individuals with vitD deficiency, increased dietary quercetin showed a tendency toward lower risk of PCa

design.excerpt: Case and control groups were compared using a two-sample t-test for continuous risk factors

ethnicity.excerpt: African-American (AA) men experience higher rates of prostate cancer (PCa)

location.excerpt: undergoing treatment at Howard University Hospital (HUH)

exposure_measurement.excerpt: used the 98.2 item Block Brief 2000 Food Frequency Questionnaires to measure dietary intake of quercetin

validated_results.title: Risk of prostate cancer in African-American men: Evidence of mixed effects of dietary quercetin by serum vitamin D status.
validated_results.reason: Original human case-control study reporting an age-adjusted odds ratio for serum 25(OH)D status and prostate cancer occurrence.

extraction.comparison_type: Normal serum vitamin D (>30 ng/ml) versus vitamin D deficiency
extraction.population: African-American men aged 40-70 with prostate cancer undergoing treatment and screening-program controls

sample_size.excerpt: Participants included 90 AA men with PCa undergoing treatment at Howard University Hospital (HUH) and 62 controls participating in HUH's free PCa screening program.
sample_size.location: abstract; total_n derived from reported group counts 90 + 62 = 152

cases.excerpt: Participants included 90 AA men with PCa undergoing treatment at Howard University Hospital (HUH) and 62 controls participating in HUH's free PCa screening program.

effect_size.excerpt: AA men (age 40-70) with normal levels of serum vitD (>30 ng/ml) had a 71% lower risk of PCa compared to AA men with vitD deficiency (OR = 0.29, 95%CI: 0.08-1.03; P = 0.055).

confidence_interval.excerpt: AA men (age 40-70) with normal levels of serum vitD (>30 ng/ml) had a 71% lower risk of PCa compared to AA men with vitD deficiency (OR = 0.29, 95%CI: 0.08-1.03; P = 0.055).

comparison.excerpt: AA men (age 40-70) with normal levels of serum vitD (>30 ng/ml) had a 71% lower risk of PCa compared to AA men with vitD deficiency

design.excerpt: Associations between risk factors and PCa risk were examined via age-adjusted logistic regression models

ethnicity.excerpt: African-American (AA) men experience higher rates of prostate cancer (PCa) and vitamin D (vitD) deficiency than white men
